objects.description: Hashing utility class that wraps SpookyHash (V2) for incremental updates over strings, fragments, raw bytes, and 64-bit integers, producing a 128-bit result. Exposes conversions to a fixed-size byte_array<2,uint64_t>, bloom filter bits, hex string, and UUID-like string. It initializes SpookyHash with seeds (0,0). Details about string_fragment, auto_buffer, byte_array, and SpookyHash are external to this header.
Type alias for a C function pointer taking a void* and returning void. Intended to denote a deallocation/free function signature.

Resizable RAII buffer managing a malloc/realloc/free-backed contiguous char array with size and capacity tracking. Supports allocation, move semantics, append/push_back, bitset helpers, growth (expand_*), slicing/iterators, release() to transfer ownership, and converting to unique_ptr. No copy semantics.
Wrapper struct tagging an auto_buffer as text-oriented. Holds an auto_buffer field named inner. Semantics beyond tagging are not specified.
Wrapper struct tagging an auto_buffer as binary/blob-oriented. Holds an auto_buffer field named inner. Semantics beyond tagging are not specified.

A non-owning view over a contiguous substring of a character buffer. Stores a base char* plus begin/end indices and provides utilities for comparison, slicing, UTF-8 navigation, tokenization, trimming, hashing, and formatting. It does not manage memory; the underlying storage must outlive the fragment. Includes nested helper structs tag1 and quoted_string_body and an enum class case_style.
Predicate helper inside string_fragment that matches a single specific character value.
Stateful predicate used to scan the body of a double-quoted string, handling backslash escapes and stopping at the closing quote.

Abstract producer that yields a sequence of string_fragment chunks. next() returns a variant of eof, a fragment, or an error. Provides a helper to iterate with a callback and a factory from(string_fragment) to create a concrete producer (implementation not shown).
Sentinel type used by string_fragment_producer to signal end of stream.
Error container used by string_fragment_producer carrying a descriptive message.

Interned string object managed by a global/central table. Provides static lookup methods to return a canonical instance for a given content. Holds the owning std::string and links to next for table chaining. Users interact via pointers to interned instances.
Forward declaration for the underlying table/type that owns and manages intern_string instances. Definition is not present in this header.
Type alias for a shared_ptr owning the intern table lifetime. Use to keep the intern table alive while in use.

Lightweight handle/wrapper for an interned string pointer. Provides string-like accessors, comparisons, hashing by pointer identity, and conversion to std::string and string_fragment. Does not own storage; nullptr represents empty.
Hasher functor for string_fragment suitable for unordered containers; hashes the fragment contents with hash_str.
Hasher functor for intern_string_t that hashes by string contents using hash_str.

functions.name: byte_array::from
functions.signature:
template <size_t COUNT, typename T = unsigned char>
static byte_array<COUNT, T> from(std::initializer_list<T> bytes)
functions.description: Constructs a byte_array<COUNT, T> from the provided initializer list by copying each element (narrowed to an unsigned byte) into the internal byte buffer in order. Remaining bytes, if any, remain zero-initialized. Intended for convenient literal initialization of the byte buffer.
requirements: bytes.size() must be <= BYTE_COUNT (COUNT * sizeof(T)); otherwise writing past the end of the internal buffer will occur.

Resulting object is returned by value; the source list is not retained.

bool operator<(const byte_array<COUNT, T>& other) const
functions.description: Lexicographical comparison of two byte_array objects based on their raw byte contents using memcmp over BYTE_COUNT bytes. Useful for ordering in associative containers.
requirements: Both objects must be valid byte_array<COUNT, T> instances with initialized storage; comparison reads exactly BYTE_COUNT bytes from each.

functions.name: byte_array::operator!=

template <size_t COUNT, typename T = unsigned char>
bool operator!=(const byte_array<COUNT, T>& other) const
functions.description: Inequality comparison based on a byte-wise comparison (memcmp) of the entire buffer. Returns true if any byte differs.
requirements: Both objects must be valid byte_array<COUNT, T> instances with initialized storage; comparison reads exactly BYTE_COUNT bytes from each.

functions.name: byte_array::operator==
functions.signature:
template <size_t COUNT, typename T = unsigned char>
bool operator==(const byte_array<COUNT, T>& other) const
functions.description: Equality comparison based on a byte-wise comparison (memcmp) of the entire buffer. Returns true only if all BYTE_COUNT bytes match.
requirements: Both objects must be valid byte_array<COUNT, T> instances with initialized storage; comparison reads exactly BYTE_COUNT bytes from each.

functions.name: byte_array::clear
functions.signature:
template <size_t COUNT, typename T = unsigned char>
void clear()
functions.description: Zeroes out the entire internal byte buffer (BYTE_COUNT bytes). Use to reset the buffer to all zeros.
requirements: The object must be a valid byte_array instance; calling clear overwrites all BYTE_COUNT bytes with zeros.

functions.name: byte_array::to_string
functions.signature:
template <size_t COUNT, typename T = unsigned char>
template <typename OutputIt>
void to_string(OutputIt out, std::optional<char> separator = std::nullopt) const
functions.description: Formats the internal bytes as lowercase hexadecimal pairs and writes them to the provided output iterator. If a separator is provided, it is inserted between bytes.
requirements: OutputIt must be a valid output iterator that accepts char output (e.g., std::back_insert_iterator<std::string>, std::ostream_iterator<char>, etc.).
Writes exactly (2 * BYTE_COUNT) hexadecimal characters plus up to (BYTE_COUNT - 1) separator characters if provided.
The byte_array must remain alive for the duration of the write; however, the function only reads from the buffer.

functions.name: byte_array::to_string
functions.signature:

std::string to_string(std::optional<char> separator = std::nullopt) const
functions.description: Returns a std::string containing the lowercase hexadecimal representation of the internal bytes. If a separator is provided, it is inserted between byte pairs.
requirements: Allocates a string of size approximately (2 * BYTE_COUNT) plus separators; callers should be aware of potential memory usage for large BYTE_COUNT values.

functions.name: byte_array::to_uuid_string
functions.signature:
template <size_t COUNT, typename T = unsigned char>
std::string to_uuid_string() const
functions.description: Returns a string formatted like a UUID (8-4-4-4-12 hex digits) using the first 16 bytes of the buffer. If fewer than 16 bytes are available, bytes are reused by index modulo BYTE_COUNT. Intended for representing 16-byte identifiers.
requirements: BYTE_COUNT must be > 0; otherwise modulo by zero occurs when indexing.
For a standard UUID representation, callers should ensure at least 16 meaningful bytes are present (i.e., BYTE_COUNT >= 16). If BYTE_COUNT < 16, the output repeats bytes due to modulo indexing.

functions.name: byte_array::in
functions.signature:
template <size_t COUNT, typename T = unsigned char>
const unsigned char* in() const
functions.description: Returns a const pointer to the internal raw byte buffer for read-only access.

The pointer must not be used to write, as it is const-qualified.

functions.name: byte_array::out
functions.signature:
template <size_t COUNT, typename T = unsigned char>

functions.description: Returns a pointer to the buffer reinterpreted as a T* advanced by offset elements. Intended for writing or accessing the buffer as an array of T elements.
requirements: offset must be within [0, COUNT] for pointer arithmetic; for dereferencing or writing, offset must be within [0, COUNT - 1].

The returned T* may have stricter alignment requirements than the underlying unsigned char buffer provides; callers must ensure alignment is suitable for T before dereferencing to avoid undefined behavior.
Access through the returned pointer must not exceed COUNT elements (i.e., do not read/write past COUNT elements).
T should be trivially copyable/compatible with raw byte storage to avoid undefined behavior when reinterpreting memory.

data_types.description: An unconstrained byte sequence. May contain any 8-bit values, including NULs and non-UTF-8 sequences. Used generically for functions that accept or process raw buffers, std::string data, or string_fragment contents without requiring a specific encoding or format.

generators.generator:
import random
import struct
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for arbitrary bytes tailored to exercise the fuzz stubs that
# consume std::string, raw bytes, and string_fragment data. We focus on
# producing valid, diverse byte sequences with varied sizes and content
# patterns that trigger different code paths while remaining within
# expected limits (<= 4096 bytes here; many stubs further clamp to <= 2048).

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

# Interesting lengths commonly used by hashing and buffer code paths
INTERESTING_LENGTHS = [
    0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 15, 16, 17, 23, 24, 31, 32, 33, 39, 40, 63, 64,
    127, 128, 255, 256, 511, 512, 1023, 1024, 1536, 2048
]

# Useful byte patterns
PAT_ZERO = bytes()
PAT_ASCII = (string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " \t\r\n").encode()

UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "", "é", "漢字", "👍", "𝔘𝔫𝔦𝔠𝔬𝔡𝔢", "привет", "مرحبا", "हिन्दी", "mañana",
]

# Repeating blocks with different periodicities
BLOCKS: List[bytes] = [
    b"", b"A", b"AB", b"ABC", b"0123456789", b"\x00\x01\x02\x03\x04\x05\x06\x07",
    b"\xff\x00\xff\x00", b"Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, ",
]

# Precompute some deterministic patterns for speed
def make_repeating(block: bytes, length: int) -> bytes:
    if not block:
        return bytes(length)
    reps, rem = divmod(length, len(block))
    return block * reps + block[:rem]


def rnd_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def mix_patterns(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Build a buffer by concatenating several segments of different kinds
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) < n:
        choice = rng.randrange(0, 8)
        remain = n - len(out)
        seg_len = min(remain, max(1, int(rng.random() ** 2 * remain)))
        if choice == 0:
            # random bytes
            out += rnd_bytes(rng, seg_len)
        elif choice == 1:
            # ASCII subset
            out += bytes(rng.choice(PAT_ASCII) for _ in range(seg_len))
        elif choice == 2:
            # zeros
            out += b"\x00" * seg_len
        elif choice == 3:
            # 0xFFs
            out += b"\xff" * seg_len
        elif choice == 4:
            # repeating small block
            blk = rng.choice(BLOCKS)
            out += make_repeating(blk, seg_len)
        elif choice == 5:
            # counters 0..255
            start = rng.randrange(0, 256)
            out += bytes(((start + i) & 0xFF) for i in range(seg_len))
        elif choice == 6:
            # alternating pattern
            a = rng.randrange(0, 256)
            b = rng.randrange(0, 256)
            out += bytes(a if (i & 1) == 0 else b for i in range(seg_len))
        else:
            # embed valid UTF-8 chunk then arbitrary tail
            s = rng.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES).encode("utf-8")
            rep = make_repeating(s, seg_len)
            # fold in a few random flips
            ba = bytearray(rep)
            flips = min(3, seg_len)
            for _ in range(flips):
                if seg_len == 0:
                    break
                idx = rng.randrange(0, seg_len)
                ba[idx] ^= rng.randrange(1, 256)
            out += bytes(ba)
    return bytes(out[:n])


def choose_length(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Bias towards interesting boundaries but allow arbitrary up to 2048
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        n = rng.choice(INTERESTING_LENGTHS)
    else:
        n = rng.randrange(0, 2049)
    # Keep within global limit
    return min(n, MAX_TOTAL)


def add_structured_prefixes(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Add a small prefix header that some stubs may copy into fixed-size
    # byte_array buffers (20/24/32/40). Not required by API but varies content.
    parts = []
    tag = rng.choice([b"BA32", b"BA24", b"BA40", b"RAW", b"STR", b"FRAG"])  # 3-4 bytes
    parts.append(tag)
    # Append a little-endian int64 to exercise hasher::update(int64_t)
    val = rng.getrandbits(64)
    parts.append(struct.pack("<Q", val))
    # Small delimiter and random few bytes
    parts.append(b"::")
    parts.append(rnd_bytes(rng, rng.randrange(0, 8)))
    return b"".join(parts)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build the buffer: optional structured prefixes + a main body sized
    # to hit the common clamp of 2048 bytes while keeping <= 4096.
    prefix = add_structured_prefixes(rng)

    # Decide on main payload count: produce 1 to 3 segments with varied patterns
    segments: List[bytes] = [prefix]
    seg_count = 1 + (rng.randrange(0, 3))
    remaining_budget = MAX_TOTAL - len(prefix)

    for _ in range(seg_count):
        if remaining_budget <= 0:
            break
        n = choose_length(rng)
        n = min(n, remaining_budget)
        # Choose a generation strategy
        kind = rng.randrange(0, 5)
        if kind == 0:
            seg = mix_patterns(rng, n)
        elif kind == 1:
            # pure ASCII text with newlines to exercise split_lines etc.
            alphabet = (string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " \t\r\n-_,.;:/\\").encode()
            seg = bytes(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))
        elif kind == 2:
            # repeating block aligned to 16
            blk = rng.choice([b"\x00" * 16, b"\xff" * 16, b"0123456789ABCDEF", b"hasher-blk-16--"])
            seg = make_repeating(blk, n)
        elif kind == 3:
            # random bytes
            seg = rnd_bytes(rng, n)
        else:
            # UTF-8 heavy content
            chosen = rng.choices(UNICODE_SAMPLES, k=max(1, n // 4))
            utf = " ".join(chosen).encode("utf-8")
            seg = make_repeating(utf, n)
        segments.append(seg)
        remaining_budget -= len(seg)

    # Ensure we provide at least some data even if lengths chose zero
    if sum(len(s) for s in segments) == 0:
        segments.append(b"\x00")

    data = b"".join(segments)
    # Trim to global limit
    if len(data) > MAX_TOTAL:
        data = data[:MAX_TOTAL]

    return data
